subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should operator `cron run` executions be strictly non-consuming while timer and Gateway watcher executions exclusively own scheduler counters, backoff, next-run state, enabled state, and one-shot deletion?
rationale: The linked issue requests this semantic change and carries a product-decision signal; source review can validate implementation mechanics but cannot establish the intended public behavior contract for manual runs.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
options.body: Approve the proposed semantics, keep scheduler origin internal, and require live proof for operator and watcher paths before merge.

options.title: Keep consuming manual runs
options.body: Retain current consumption semantics and instead add an explicit safe verification or deletion-override workflow with clear user feedback.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed semantics, keep scheduler origin internal, and require live proof for operator and watcher paths before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the cron service and its public Gateway/service contract makes this the best available owner for the behavior and API-boundary choice.
